status_summary: USAID, whose staff, missions and country strategies the text addresses, closed on 2025-07-01, and the executive record in the successor structure mostly runs the other way: CRS reported (2026-06-03) that a significant portion of congressionally directed religious freedom programs were terminated after the early 2025 aid pause, that the Office of International Religious Freedom moved back under the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, that the ambassador-at-large nomination was returned to the President, and that the nominee left his advisory role in April 2026 with no new nomination announced. The House Appropriations Committee summary of the FY2026 State appropriations enacted in Public Law 119-75 (2026-02-03) says the law increases support for religious freedom programs and restricts assistance to Nigeria until steps are taken to protect Christian communities, but the enacted text was not read and no line specific to persecuted religious minorities was confirmed. Other steps are parallel: State's foreign assistance powers were delegated on 2025-08-21 to an Under Secretary whose title includes Religious Freedom, Nigeria was designated a Country of Particular Concern on 2025-10-31, a visa restriction policy for religious freedom violators was announced in December 2025 (CRS), and State announced nearly $2 billion in health and humanitarian awards to faith-based organizations on 2026-08-06 (DevelopmentAid). No staff training or integration of religious freedom into aid programs was found, so the record is placed at proposed, with the appropriations element unconfirmed in statutory text.

timeline.event: State published a delegation of foreign assistance powers to an Under Secretary whose title includes Religious Freedom; the text names no international religious freedom office.
The President announced Nigeria's designation as a Country of Particular Concern; CRS reported no resulting action had been announced.
An analysis republished by allAfrica noted that the President had threatened to cut aid to Nigeria and that past designations were seldom followed by sanctions.

Public Law 119-75 was enacted; the House Appropriations Committee's undated summary of the final State bill says it increases support for religious freedom programs and restricts assistance to Nigeria until measurable steps protect Christian communities.

CRS reported that a significant portion of programs using congressionally directed religious freedom funds were terminated after the 2025 aid pause (citing USCIRF), that the Office of International Religious Freedom returned to the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor in the 2025 reorganization, that the ambassador nomination was returned to the President, and that a visa restriction policy for religious freedom violators was announced in December 2025.

A report on a State release of 2026-08-06 described nearly $2 billion in health and humanitarian awards to faith-based organizations under the America First Global Health Strategy; the report does not mention religious freedom.

title: Make religious freedom central to development aid and fund persecuted minorities
uncertainties: The text of the FY2026 appropriations law was not read for religious freedom lines: on 2026-10-18 the GovInfo HTML of Public Law 119-75 again ended at about 133,000 characters, before Division F, and a targeted search found no separate copy of that division, so the House committee summary is the only basis; it gives no dollar figure and prints no date. The CRS report of 2026-06-03 gives no FY2026 amounts and does not mention persecuted religious minorities or Executive Order 13926. Whether any FY2026 line is specific to persecuted religious minorities was not confirmed. No revocation of Executive Order 13926 was found, and whether its $50 million budgeting target is met was not confirmed. Delegation No. 597 names religious freedom only in the Under Secretary's title and lists no religious freedom functions. The faith-based awards concern health and humanitarian delivery and rest on a news report of a State release, since state.gov could not be reached. The stage is a judgment call: in_progress 25 would be defensible if the committee summary is taken as proof of an operative aligned appropriation, and diverged would be defensible given the program terminations and the office's move back under a bureau.
